claim: For the bivariate-failure-extropy dependence index \(D\) proposed by Pandey and Kundu, \(D=0\) does not characterize independence. There is an absolutely continuous copula with uniform margins whose \(3\times3\) checkerboard cell-probability matrix is \(P=1089^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}265&49&49\\13&49&301\\85&265&13\end{pmatrix}\). It is nonindependent, yet its bivariate failure extropy equals the independence benchmark: \(J=J_0=1/36\), hence \(D=0\). Its Spearman coefficient is \(\rho_S=64/363\ne0\).
integrity: The cell table, copula integrals, BFEx value, and Spearman coefficient are proved with exact rational arithmetic and piecewise-polynomial integration; no simulation is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The result disproves only the implication from zero BFEx dependence index to independence; it does not classify the full zero set or assess estimator performance.
The explicit counterexample is an absolutely continuous checkerboard copula with a piecewise-constant density; no smooth-density version is claimed.
An equivalent counterexample under older information-measure terminology remains a residual literature risk.
title: A checkerboard copula with zero BFEx dependence index but nonzero Spearman dependence
